vulnerabilities.title: Unencrypted Session Storage
vulnerabilities.description: Session data including working directory, user context, and metrics are stored in plain JSON without encryption.
vulnerabilities.risk: An attacker with file system access can read sensitive session information and execution context.

vulnerabilities.title: Unencrypted Memory Database
vulnerabilities.description: Memory key-value pairs stored in plain JSON format without encryption.
vulnerabilities.risk: All stored memory data is readable in plain text to any user with file system access.

vulnerabilities.title: No Input Validation on Memory Values
vulnerabilities.description: Values stored in memory are not validated. Could lead to XSS if used in web context without sanitization.
vulnerabilities.risk: If stored values are displayed in HTML without escaping, XSS attacks become possible.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Temporary File Handling
vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files created with randomness but written to disk, creating a time window where sensitive content is exposed.
vulnerabilities.risk: Sensitive content temporarily written to disk; vulnerable to privileged process inspection during creation.

vulnerabilities.title: No File Permissions Check in Database Access
vulnerabilities.description: Code attempts to read database files without proper error handling, risking information disclosure.
vulnerabilities.risk: Error messages or stack traces might reveal sensitive file paths or database structure.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Explicit CSP Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: Google Analytics script loaded without explicit Content Security Policy handling.
vulnerabilities.risk: While Next.js handles this reasonably, explicit CSP headers would provide additional protection.

strengths: ✓ No hardcoded API keys or secrets in source code
✓ Correct use of NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix for public environment variables
✓ Use of spawnSync prevents command injection vulnerabilities
✓ Key format validation in memory and session modules
✓ Proper error handling with try-catch blocks
✓ Use of path.join() prevents directory traversal attacks

critical_findings.hardcoded_secrets: PASS - No API keys, passwords, or tokens found
critical_findings.command_injection: PASS - Uses spawnSync, not shell execution

recommendations.action: Implement AES-256 encryption for session and memory storage in .claude/helpers/
Add schema validation for memory values using Zod or Joi
Replace custom temp file handling with Node.js tmp module
Add comprehensive error handling and sanitization in statusline.js
Document CSP headers in next.config.js and verify GTM domain whitelisting

conclusion: The Calculo Gratis codebase has strong security fundamentals with no critical injection vulnerabilities or hardcoded secrets. The main security concerns relate to unencrypted storage of session and memory data, which should be encrypted at rest. Addressing the HIGH priority recommendations will significantly improve the security posture.
